Subject: Greencore performance playbook kickoff and MAP proposal

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the run through last week. As discussed, we put together a compact mutual action playbook that bundles the evaluation plan + measurable close milestones so both teams can track progress. High level goals: validate latency/throughput profiles across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments, exercise autoscaling and isolation under Greencore traffic patterns, and confirm a recommended serving configuration for production.

Proposed scope (attached):
- MAP item 1: Controlled benchmark runs (TTFT, p50/p95/p99 latency, sustained throughput) across the three hosting modes.
- MAP item 2: Concurrency ramp tests with step increases to observe autoscale thresholds and cold-start behavior.
- MAP item 3: Isolation stress window: run background noisy tenants to validate tail latency on Dedicated and Private.
- MAP item 4: End-to-end acceptance criteria to unblock procurement (quantified SLOs and cost envelope).

Can we lock the test window for Apr 6–9? If that works I’ll assign owners and share the harness access. Also attaching the draft playbook and a quick csv template so you can add your sample load profile.

Next steps:
1) Sarah to confirm test window and provide traffic profile.
2) Greencore to sign the MAP doc (DocuSign link in the drive).
3) Redwood to provision Dedicated sandbox + private VPC lab and provide credentials.

Thanks,
Mina

Quick tech notes for the test harness and what we'll capture in the CSV:
- Measurements: TTFT, token-generation throughput (tokens/sec), sustained request/sec at target QPS, p50/p95/p99 latency (server-side), cold-start latency, and CPU/GPU utilization per replica.
- Autoscale triggers: we will run tests that exercise both queue-depth based autoscaling and latency-SLO based autoscaling. For Dedicated we’ll also toggle fixed-pool vs. burst modes.
- Isolation tests: plan to run a noisy tenant at 60–80% background load for 2 x 30-minute windows while Greencore traffic runs baseline and peak shapes. We will collect percentiles and tail behavior.

I’ll provision the Dedicated sandbox and the Private VPC lab. Need Greencore to provide the SSH key + the load profile (already on drive).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@greencore.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Greencore MAP — summary of benchmark results (first-pass)

Sarah / team —

Attached is the first-pass summary (map-benchmark-summary-20270413.csv) and a quick chart comparing p95 latency and steady-state throughput across hosting modes. High-level findings:

- Hosted (Redwood managed):
  - p50/p95/p99 latency for chat test: 42ms / 120ms / 320ms
  - TTFT median: 72ms
  - Sustained tokens/sec (single model): ~5.6k tokens/sec at 50 concurrent streams
  - Autoscale behavior: fast warm pool reuse, essentially no VM cold-starts during our windows; consistent 99th percentile under synthetic load.

- Dedicated (reserved pool, fixed-pool mode):
  - p50/p95/p99 latency: 38ms / 110ms / 280ms (slightly better p50 due to isolated GPUs)
  - TTFT median: 68ms
  - Sustained tokens/sec: ~6.2k tokens/sec at 50 concurrent streams
  - Autoscale: in fixed-pool mode, we saw predictable throughput but limited headroom; in burst mode, cold-start to new spot-like nodes added ~1.1s tail spikes during very aggressive ramps.

- Private VPC lab (network-limited by partner NAT to 1Gbps):
  - p50/p95/p99 latency: 45ms / 140ms / 410ms (network egress cap is visible in p99)
  - TTFT median: 95ms (extra network hop and NAT)
  - Sustained tokens/sec: capped by 1Gbps egress, ~4.8k tokens/sec
  - Isolation: under noisy-tenant run, Dedicated showed <5% p95 degradation, Private saw up to 18% p95 degradation when background tenant saturated egress.

Risk / notes:
- Private test results are not indicative of a properly provisioned Greencore on-prem deployment — the NAT cap affected aggregate throughput and tail latency. For procurement we should exclude the NAT-limited runs or re-run in a fully provisioned on-prem lab.
- We captured TTFT for chat as requested; it correlates with attention span distribution and kernel choices.

Proposed acceptance criteria to unblock procurement:
- Chat TTFT median <= 85ms for the chosen deployment mode (Hosted or Dedicated).
- p95 latency under baseline load <= 140ms.
- Autoscale: no sustained >1s tail spikes at normal ramp rates (canary ramp: +10%/min up to +200%).

Attached: map-benchmark-summary-20270413.csv, latency-comparison-chart.png, and the MAP action-items doc. Please review — if acceptable we’ll update the MAP and push for Procurement sign-off this week.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer | Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@greencore.com>

Karthik —

Thank you for the detailed summary and for capturing TTFT — that was the most important metric for our product team. A couple quick responses:
1) We will re-run the Private test in our lab (no NAT cap) — procurement wants a dedicated on-prem number before committing. Can Redwood help schedule an on-site validation week (May 3–7)?
2) For the acceptance criteria, procurement is okay with the TTFT ≤ 85ms if that is validated in our on-prem lab. Please add a clause to the MAP for a re-test window and for cost reconciliation if we observe >10% variance.
3) We’ll sign the MAP conditional on the re-test clause.

Next steps:
- Mina to update the MAP doc and include the re-test clause + DocuSign.
- Marissa / Karthik to propose a final configuration (Hosted vs Dedicated) with cost bands by Apr 20.
- Procurement will prepare a term sheet once MAP is signed.

I’ve attached a short note from procurement about cost modeling. Once the MAP includes the re-test clause we can move to signature.

—Sarah
